newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Scania says market view supported by strong July.
newsitem.headline: Scania says market view supported by strong July.

text.p: Swedish truckmaker Scania said on Monday it had its strongest ever July in terms of new orders, supporting its view that the market had turned up.

"The month of July has been very good and historically the best that we have had...This supports our view that the trend seems to have changed," Scania managing director Leif Ostling told a news conference.
"The operating profit has (also) turned around...but there still is a way until we reach levels from the beginning of 1996," Ostling said.
Ostling said prices had turned upwards in Latin America but fallen in Europe. Prices for the company's 4-series truck were now one to two percent lower in Europe compared to one year ago.
"We have a more positive view on South America than we had a half year ago," Ostling said, adding that he believed prices would stabilise in Europe.
"After a certain lag we expect a stabilisation in Europe," said Ostling without specifying when such stabilisation could be expected.
Scania said its profit after financial items dropped 36 percent to 1.35 billion crowns in the first six months of the year, less than the 1.43 billion crowns analysts in a Reuter poll had targeted.
